title: Three Nights and One Short Wick
subtitle: 火灾安全 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 火灾安全（灾害防范·火灾与安全）
meta: 主题语境：火灾安全（灾害防范·火灾与安全）　|　核心词汇：flame　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 flame 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the keeper ① lit a flame that no neighbour in the hall would have watched, and he said the lighting was the whole of the night. The ② flame, meaning the fire itself and not the smoke, ran three nights and stayed unwatched in the book; a flame, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left unwatched.

Every ③ flame in that hall had the same short wick beside it, and the ④ flame at the far end, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A flame, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to watch; the keeper said the watching is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the flame was the whole of the matter, meaning the passion and not the fire. The ⑥ flame, meaning the passion and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody watches; flame, he said, is either something you light or the only word that means both a fire and a passion. He said the passion is the part they remember.

By 1973 the ⑦ flame had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short wick. The ⑧ flame of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in January, was one hall and three nights of watching; flame, he said, is either the one at the far end or the reason you learned to watch. He said the watching was never mentioned.

The ⑨ flame I remember is the one written in the plan, which closed in 1975 and is still described as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ flame, my mother said in 1977, is the only one that improves by being watched; every flame, she said, is a passion that has agreed to look like a fire. She said the passion was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 火焰；火苗（指厅里每一处旁边的那一处）
B. n. 火焰（指那一处本身，与烟相对）
C. 固定搭配：light a flame 点燃一处火苗
D. n. 火焰（指留给孩子们的那一处）
E. n. 火焰（抽象总称，指一座厅堂的燃火之事）
F. n. 火焰（指计划里写到、被人看过的那一处）
G. n. 激情；热恋（旧用法，指一件事里人人都等却无人看过的那样东西）
H. n. 激情（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人看过的那样东西）

items.q: lit a flame that no neighbour in the hall would have watched
The flame, meaning the fire itself and not the smoke
the flame at the far end
the flame was the whole of the matter
the flame had become a line in a plan
The flame of the whole thing
A flame, my mother said in 1977

answers.why: light a flame 意为“点燃一处火苗”，1966 年那位看守人点燃了一处厅里没有一位邻居肯看守的火苗。
flame 意为“火焰”，指那一处本身而不是烟，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有人看守。
flame 意为“火焰”，指厅里每一处旁边的那一处，每一处旁边都有同一根短短的灯芯。
flame 意为“火焰”，指留给孩子们的那一处，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
flame 意为“激情、热恋”，指一件事里人人都等却无人看过的那样东西，叔叔说这份激情就是那件事的全部。
flame 意为“激情”，指人人都等却无人看过的那样东西而不是那一处火焰，是事情里人人都等、却无人看过的东西。
flame 意为“火焰”，指计划里写到、被人看过的那一处，到 1973 年这一处成了计划里的一行。
flame 意为“火焰”，看守人一月写道，整件事的燃火之事是一座厅堂和三个夜晚的看守。
flame 意为“火焰”，我记得的是计划里写下的那一处，1975 年结束了，至今仍被说成厅里最安静的一处。
flame 为抽象总称，母亲 1977 年说，一处火焰是唯一会因为被好好看守而变得更好的东西。
